predictions.experiment: Pool fresh base samples with seeds independent of Day-1 #3 sample 0 and count how many of the 17 RL-solved base-0/4 problems get at least one right answer.
predictions.recipe: Problems: entries of studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json key `problems` with base_k == 0 and rl_k >= 1. Pool per problem (index = problem_index): (a) studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl rows with attempt in {1, 2}, score_v3; (b) studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json, the arm whose manifest.json job id is abaybektursun-1114-153047-6429 (random matched-norm difference, cue), its 0/1 at the problem's position in problem_indices; (c) the same file, the arm with job id abaybektursun-1114-183855-e840 (base-written examples), absent for problems not in its problem_indices; (d) iterate-runs:frustea-1114-180853-e383/answers.jsonl rows with attempt 0 (or no attempt field), score_v3; (e) s3 r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl, every row (all samples), with v3 recomputed by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py from text and gold; (f) studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/screen100/base_cue-01/per_problem.json score_v3 (problems 0-99 only). Leave out every other source. A problem counts as solved if any pooled sample has v3 score 1. Cap hits count as wrong (their score as stored or recomputed); a missing source or row adds nothing. Statistic: solved problems / 17.
predictions.note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json (class base_k == 0 and rl_k >= 1); (a) results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl rows with attempt 1 or 2 (restarts after cap hits; 90 + 47 rows in the whole file, so only problems whose samples hit the cap get any), stored score_v3; (b) results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json arm random_cue (manifest job abaybektursun-1114-153047-6429); (c) arm shots_base (job -183855-e840), None entries (problems 0-2) treated as absent; (d) runs/theory-tests/frustea-1114-180853-e383/answers.jsonl (Modal iterate-runs, T 1.5 min-p 0.1), attempt 0 rows, stored score_v3; (e) runs/theory-tests/s3/F_math500.jsonl (S3 r3/base-01, T 0.6 top-p 0.95, one row per problem, sample 0 only), v3 recomputed with rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text), which is what grader/rln4_grader_v3.py calls (its JUDGED_INCORRECT hand list is report-only and not applied); (f) results/wsp1/screen100/base_cue-01/per_problem.json score_v3. Solved = any pooled score == 1; cap hits keep their stored/recomputed score. Denominator is the literal 17; if the class turns out not to have 17 members the number is off (stderr prints the class size). Ambiguity and alt_measured: source (d) uses seed 41,000,000 + i, the same per-request seed as Day-1 #3 sample 0, which the theory's scope says to leave out (it lists only T1, b614, 456c, but e383 has the same seed at T 1.5); alt_measured drops (d). Note the pool mixes T 0.6 (e) and T 1.5 (d) samples with T 1.0 ones, as the recipe says. If a fetch fails, the script reports not_computable rather than silently counting the source as empty.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test against the dose-scaling / new-solution rival: the pooled solve fraction on the 17 RL-solved base-0/4 problems minus the same fraction on the 16 base-0/4 problems RL never solves. The rival (RL creates paths where the base's p is about 0) predicts a difference of about 0.00; this theory predicts a clearly positive one.
predictions.recipe: Use the pool, solve rule, cap-hit and missing-row rules of the first prediction. A = solved / 17 over pool_k_le3.json problems with base_k == 0 and rl_k >= 1; B = solved / 16 over problems with base_k == 0 and rl_k == 0. Statistic: A - B (if the class sizes differ from 17 / 16, divide by the actual class sizes).
predictions.refuted_by: A - B measured at or below 0.0
predictions.note: Same files, pool and rules as k=1. A = solved / |rl_k >= 1 class|, B = solved / |rl_k == 0 class| over base_k == 0 problems of pool_k_le3.json, using the actual class sizes (expected 17 and 16). Refuted if A - B <= 0.0. An empty class gives not_computable (the recipe does not say an empty class refutes). alt_measured: A - B with source (d) (frustea e383, same per-request seed as Day-1 #3 sample 0) left out. Problems 0-99 get one extra sample from (f) and problems 0-2 lack (c), so per-problem sample counts differ between classes; with about 6-10 samples per problem this difference in pool size, not only base rates, can move A - B.

predictions.experiment: Per-sample base success rate in the independent pool on the 17 RL-solved base-0/4 problems: the mechanism says 'a few percent' per sample, not about 0 and not near the base's overall 0.82.
predictions.recipe: Same 17 problems and the same sources (a)-(f) as the first prediction. Each pooled row or arm entry present for the problem is one sample (a vectors.json arm entry is 1 sample; F_math500 rows count one per row). Statistic: total samples with v3 score 1 / total samples present, summed over the 17 problems (a pooled ratio, not a mean of per-problem rates). Cap hits count as wrong samples; missing sources add no samples.
predictions.note: Same 17 problems and sources as k=1. Samples: every Day-1 #3 row with attempt 1 or 2, one entry per vectors.json arm where not None, every e383 attempt-0 row, every F_math500 row, every screen100 per_problem row. Statistic: sum of right / number of samples, pooled over problems (not a mean of per-problem rates). Cap hits count as wrong samples (stored or recomputed score). alt_measured drops source (d) (same per-request seed as Day-1 #3 sample 0, at T 1.5). The Day-1 #3 sample 0-3 attempt-0 rows are not in the pool (the recipe takes only attempts 1 and 2); including them would add 68 wrong samples and lower the rate a lot. Restart rows exist only for problems whose samples hit the cap, so these problems are weighted by their cap-hit count. stderr prints n and right per source.
